intro.say: All living things start small, grow and change. This is called a life cycle!

rounds.say: A seed grows into a sprout, then a plant, then a big sunflower. The flower makes new seeds!
rounds.caption: seed → sprout → plant → flower

rounds.say: People grow too! A baby becomes a child, then a grown-up, and one day an older person.
rounds.caption: baby → child → grown-up → older

rounds.ask: Put the person growing up in order, youngest first.
rounds.explain: We start as babies, grow into children, then grown-ups, then older people.

rounds.ask: A sprout grows into a plant. What comes next?

options.label: Seed
options.why: The seed came at the start.

options.label: Dry leaf
options.why: A healthy plant keeps growing first.

options.label: Grandad
options.why: Grandad has grown for a long time.

options.label: Child
options.why: Someone here is even younger.

rounds.explain: A baby is at the very start of growing up.

rounds.ask: What does a flower make, to start new plants?

options.label: Rocks
options.why: Rocks are not alive.

options.label: Leaves
options.why: Leaves help a plant make food.

rounds.explain: A flower makes seeds, and each seed can grow a new plant.

rounds.ask: Which one does NOT have a life cycle?

options.label: Sunflower
options.why: A sunflower grows from a seed.

options.label: Frog
options.why: A frog grows from an egg.

rounds.explain: A rock is not alive. It does not grow or have babies.

rounds.ask: A baby grows into a child. What does a child grow into?

options.label: Baby
options.why: Babies are younger than children.

options.label: Puppy
options.why: People grow into people.

intro.say: A frog changes so much as it grows! Let us follow every stage, step by step.

rounds.say: Frog eggs are called frogspawn. A tiny tadpole hatches. It swims with its tail and breathes under water with gills.
rounds.caption: Frogspawn, then tadpole

rounds.say: The tadpole grows back legs, then front legs. Its tail shrinks and it becomes a froglet. Then it is a frog that hops and breathes air!
rounds.caption: Legs grow, tail shrinks

rounds.ask: Put the frog's life cycle in order.
rounds.explain: Frogspawn, tadpole, tadpole with legs, froglet, and then a frog.
rounds.hint: It starts with eggs in the water.

rounds.ask: What comes after the tadpole with legs?

options.label: Frogspawn
options.why: Frogspawn comes at the very start.

options.label: Tadpole
options.why: The tadpole came before the legs grew.

rounds.explain: Next it becomes a froglet, a little frog with a short tail.

options.label: In a tree
options.why: Tadpoles swim in water. They cannot climb trees.

options.label: In sand
options.why: A tadpole needs water to breathe.

rounds.explain: Tadpoles live in ponds. They breathe under water with gills.

rounds.ask: What does a tadpole lose as it grows into a frog?

options.label: Its eyes
options.why: A frog still has eyes.

options.label: Its mouth
options.why: A frog needs its mouth to eat.

rounds.explain: The tail gets shorter and shorter until it is gone.

rounds.ask: A hen sits on her eggs. Why?

options.label: To keep them cold
options.why: Eggs need warmth to grow.

options.label: To make them wet
options.why: Eggs need warmth, not water.

rounds.explain: The chick grows inside the egg, and it needs to be kept warm.

rounds.ask: What is a caterpillar's main job?

options.label: Fly
options.why: It cannot fly yet. That comes later.

options.label: Lay eggs
options.why: The grown-up butterfly lays eggs.

rounds.explain: A caterpillar eats lots of leaves and grows bigger and bigger.

intro.say: Life cycles go round and round. Grown-ups make new babies, and it starts again!

rounds.say: An apple seed grows into a tree. The tree grows blossom. The blossom becomes apples with seeds inside. And round it goes again!
rounds.caption: seed → tree → blossom → apple → seed

rounds.say: Some animals change shape completely, like butterflies, ladybirds and frogs. Others just grow bigger, like puppies, turtles and people.
rounds.caption: Big change, or just growing

rounds.ask: After the blossom on an apple tree, what comes next?

options.label: A dry leaf
options.why: Leaves fall in autumn. They are not part of making seeds.

options.label: A rock
options.why: Rocks do not grow on trees.

rounds.explain: The blossom turns into apples, and the apples hold new seeds.

rounds.ask: Put the apple tree's life cycle in order.
rounds.explain: Seed, sprout, tree, blossom, and then apples with new seeds.

rounds.ask: Which animal changes the most as it grows up?

options.label: Elephant
options.why: A baby elephant looks like a small elephant.

options.label: Dog
options.why: A puppy looks like a small dog.

rounds.explain: A butterfly starts as a caterpillar, then a chrysalis. It changes completely!

rounds.ask: Does it change shape completely, or just grow bigger?
rounds.explain: Frogs, ladybirds and bees change shape completely. Dogs, elephants, turtles and horses just grow bigger.
rounds.hint: Does the baby look like the grown-up?

rounds.ask: What does a grown-up butterfly do that starts the cycle again?

options.label: Makes a chrysalis
options.why: The caterpillar makes the chrysalis.

options.label: Eats leaves
options.why: The caterpillar eats leaves.

rounds.explain: A butterfly lays eggs, and new caterpillars hatch. The cycle starts again!

rounds.ask: A tadpole breathes with gills. What does a grown-up frog breathe with?

options.label: Gills
options.why: The frog loses its gills as it grows.

options.label: Leaves
options.why: Leaves belong to plants.

rounds.explain: A grown-up frog breathes air with lungs, and a little through its skin too.
